contentTypes.name: Anti-fraud education
contentTypes.description: Explain observable romance-scam patterns and safer reference actions without declaring that a person is a scammer.
contentTypes.goal: Build trust through practical dating-safety education.
contentTypes.example: A sudden money request matters more when it follows fast intimacy and weeks of avoided video calls. One clue is not a verdict. A cluster is a reason to slow down, verify independently, and keep account access private.
contentTypes.recommendedCta: Save this and share it with someone who dates online.

contentTypes.name: Product demonstration
contentTypes.description: Show how DateXray turns an invented dating conversation into an evidence-first signal review.
contentTypes.goal: Make the product concrete without exposing real user conversations.
contentTypes.example: We tested DateXray with an invented chat: fast affection, no video calls, then a crypto pitch. The report did not label the person. It surfaced the three observable patterns and the exact lines behind them.
contentTypes.recommendedCta: Try a private conversation check at datexray.com.

contentTypes.name: Build in public
contentTypes.description: Share a shipped change, the product reason behind it, and a specific lesson from building DateXray.
contentTypes.goal: Build credibility through transparent, fact-based progress updates.
contentTypes.example: Today we moved DateXray's full report data behind a one-time unlock. The lesson: a paywall is not only a UI state. Sensitive evidence should stay off the browser until access is actually granted.
contentTypes.recommendedCta: What would you want to see us build next?

contentTypes.name: Opinion
contentTypes.description: State a clear, defensible view about dating safety, AI judgment, privacy, or responsible product design.
contentTypes.goal: Give the account a recognizable point of view and invite thoughtful discussion.
contentTypes.example: Dating-safety AI should show its evidence, not hand down a verdict. A useful tool makes patterns easier to inspect while leaving the decision with the person who knows the full context.
contentTypes.recommendedCta: Where would you draw the line?

contentTypes.name: Interaction
contentTypes.description: Ask one focused question that helps people compare experiences or test a safety idea without requesting private conversations.
contentTypes.goal: Create useful replies and learn the audience's real concerns.
contentTypes.example: Which dating-app signal deserves more attention: a profile that changed overnight, a month of avoided video calls, or pressure to move the chat off-platform immediately? Why?
contentTypes.recommendedCta: Reply with the pattern you think people miss most.

contentTypes.name: Founder perspective
contentTypes.description: Tell a first-person story about a product choice, uncertainty, or lesson while clearly speaking as DateXray's builder.
contentTypes.goal: Make the account human without inventing customer stories or pretending to be an independent user.
contentTypes.example: I am building DateXray around a constraint I do not want to compromise: the tool can point to risk signals, but it should never make a relationship decision for you. Useful AI needs a boundary, not just a bigger prompt.
contentTypes.recommendedCta: I would value your perspective as we keep building.
